def adjust_for_corporate_actions(quotes, corporate_actions):
    adjusted_quotes = quotes.copy()
    for index, row in corporate_actions.iterrows():
        date = row['date']
        ticker = row['ticker']
        kind = row['kind']
        value = row['value']
        
        if kind == 'split':
            split_ratio = 1 / value
            adjusted_quotes.loc[(adjusted_quotes['date'] >= date) & (adjusted_quotes['ticker'] == ticker), 'close'] *= split_ratio
        elif kind == 'dividend':
            adjusted_quotes.loc[(adjusted_quotes['date'] >= date) & (adjusted_quotes['ticker'] == ticker), 'close'] -= value
    
    return adjusted_quotes

# Adjust the quotes for corporate actions
adjusted_quotes = adjust_for_corporate_actions(quotes, corporate_actions)

# Calculate returns
returns = adjusted_quotes.groupby('ticker')['close'].pct_change().dropna()

# Calculate the covariance matrix
cov_matrix = returns.cov()

inv_cov_matrix = np.linalg.inv(cov_matrix)

# Calculate the mean returns
mean_returns = returns.mean()

# Calculate the portfolio weights using the minimum variance formula
weights = inv_cov_matrix @ mean_returns / (mean_returns.T @ inv_cov_matrix @ mean_returns)

# Normalize the weights to sum to 1
weights = weights / weights.sum()

# Create a dictionary of weights
weights_dict = dict(zip(returns.columns, weights))

# Submit the weights
submit(weights_dict)
